primary_source.title: A higher Gross-Zagier formula and the structure of Selmer groups
primary_source.author: Chan-Ho Kim
primary_source.published_form: Transactions of the American Mathematical Society 377 (2024), 3691-3725
selectors: Introduction 1.1, especially the higher-rank number-field disclaimer
Introduction 1.4 on non-triviality of Kolyvagin systems
verified_claims: The paper calls its result a structural refinement: it compares Heegner-point Kolyvagin-system divisibilities with Kurihara-number/discrete data and Selmer structure, rather than proving a higher complex-derivative Gross-Zagier formula over number fields.
The introduction explicitly states that for rank larger than one no analogous number-field higher Gross-Zagier result is addressed, contrasting the function-field Yun-Zhang theory.

Under Theorem 2.3 hypotheses and non-triviality assumptions, the Heegner Kolyvagin-system order and Kurihara-number orders recover the relevant p-infinity Selmer coranks. This is a sharp arithmetic/discrete structure theorem once those source-side objects are available.
Remark 2.4 describes the discrete derivative operators as playing the role of Taylor coefficients only conceptually; it does not identify them with the complex Taylor coefficients of L(E,s) at s=1.

Theorem 2.2 obtains required non-triviality statements from localized Iwasawa/main-conjecture inputs; Section 2.5 separately notes unconditional low-analytic-rank non-triviality sources in analytic rank at most one.
strict_nonclaims: Theorem 2.3 does not prove that exact complex analytic rank two forces Heegner Kolyvagin-system vanishing order exactly one.
Theorem 2.3 does not prove that exact complex analytic rank two forces the relevant Kurihara/discrete order to be exactly two.
The structural higher Gross-Zagier identity does not identify a nonzero complex second derivative L''(E,1) with a first nonzero derived Heegner/Kolyvagin class in the number-field setting.
The theorem does not produce the transverse nonzero p-local localization required by the active A1a2 interface.
The theorem does not close Sha finiteness, regulator nondegeneracy, Tamagawa/torsion factors, all-prime arithmetic, or the complex BSD leading coefficient.

companion_primary_source.title: The structure of Selmer groups and the Iwasawa main conjecture for elliptic curves
companion_primary_source.author: Chan-Ho Kim
companion_primary_source.verified_claim: For arbitrary rank, exact p-infinity Selmer structure can be encoded by Kurihara numbers once their non-triviality is supplied; the bridge is through Iwasawa/refined-Iwasawa and discrete modular-symbol coordinates, not an identity from exact complex Taylor order two to the required discrete order.

current_frontier_cross_check.title: A higher Gross-Zagier type formula for moduli of shtukas at deeper level

current_frontier_cross_check.verified_claim: The 2026 higher-derivative theorem returned by the bounded current search is a function-field shtuka result extending Yun-Zhang, not a number-field elliptic-curve theorem.

counterexample_first_route_test.candidate_route: Use Kim's higher Gross-Zagier theorem as the missing sharp upper-bound step after the R9 Zhang lower bound.
counterexample_first_route_test.falsifier: Check whether the theorem's left input is the exact complex Taylor order/leading derivative, or instead an arithmetic/discrete Kolyvagin/Kurihara order whose exact value already determines Selmer corank.
counterexample_first_route_test.observation: The theorem is in the second category. Its sharp equalities classify Selmer structure from arithmetic/discrete orders; they do not derive those orders from exact complex analytic rank two.

route_result.refined_missing_transition: exact complex analytic rank two -> sharp first nonzero arithmetic/discrete derivative coordinate (e.g. Heegner-Kolyvagin order exactly one or an equivalent Kurihara-order witness) in a scope compatible with the R9 Zhang cell
